Beta hosting decided by Owner (2026-11-02): Cloudflare Workers Free runs the API and web UI; Neon Free provides PostgreSQL, reached from Workers through Hyperdrive Free; Supabase was evaluated and kept as a fully compatible alternative. Portability rules are binding: (1) only deploy/cloudflare/src/entry.py knows about Cloudflare - no Cloudflare-proprietary APIs (D1/KV/Durable Objects) in core logic; (2) persistence uses standard SQL and widely-available PostgreSQL extensions only, no Neon/Supabase platform extras (their Auth/Storage/Realtime) in the product core; (3) the app stays stateless, all durable state in PostgreSQL; daily development and tests use a local database, Neon is reserved for the shared beta/staging environments (separate Neon project per environment, compute kept at the 0.25 CU minimum). Rationale: the whole beta stack costs 0; PostgreSQL-to-PostgreSQL migration between Neon and Supabase, or out to a VPS/AWS/Azure/GCP running the same ASGI app under uvicorn, stays a pg_dump/pg_restore operation. Deployment packaging prepared in deploy/cloudflare/ with runbook docs/DEPLOY_CLOUDFLARE_NEON.md; actual deployment awaits the Owner's Cloudflare and Neon accounts. DEPLOYED 2026-11-02: the API is live at https://iaict-core-platform.iaict-coreplatform-mhy.workers.dev (Cloudflare account subdomain iaict-coreplatform-mhy; deployed via uv run pywrangler deploy after the browser-OAuth route failed on wrangler's ~2-minute authorization window and the Owner chose the one-time API-token route; the token was used transiently and never stored). Live verification: /health 200 with env=beta, deny-by-default 400/403/503 responses, tenant creation 201 with a temporary platform secret that was deleted right after the check (platform administration stays disabled at 503 until the Owner sets their own PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY secret). Verified platform constraint: in-memory state is per-isolate and is not shared between Worker requests, so multi-request flows only become meaningful when the T-004 PostgreSQL layer lands - as planned. PERSISTENCE WIRING (2026-11-02): the Owner created the Neon project (ap-southeast-1, PostgreSQL 18.6) and shared the direct connection string transiently (never stored). Verified from this environment over Neon's HTTPS SQL endpoint (the VM proxy intercepts raw TCP/5432): credentials valid, all 12 schema tables applied, cross-tenant FK rejection reproduced on Neon itself (SQLSTATE 23503). Worker-side driver settled by spike tests against Cloudflare's official Python+Hyperdrive guidance: asyncpg is recommended but its Pyodide wheel is served from a CDN unreachable from this build environment, and direct-to-Neon connections from Python Workers fail on TLS over the socket shim - which is exactly what Hyperdrive exists to solve (plaintext local leg, ssl=False). Chosen driver: pg8000 (pure Python, on Cloudflare's supported list). app/workerstore.py implements the store contract on pg8000; app/store.py gained a LazyWorkerStore selected by the Workers entrypoint (IAICT_BACKEND=hyperdrive) that binds the Hyperdrive config from the first request env and otherwise falls back to in-memory storage, reported openly by /health (storage field). Full suite passes 31/31 in all three modes (memory, psycopg, pg8000) against real PostgreSQL. The updated app is deployed to the beta (currently storage: memory). ONE step remains, with the Owner: create the Hyperdrive configuration - the current API token is denied Hyperdrive access (error 10000), so the Owner creates it in the dashboard (Workers & Pages -> Hyperdrive -> Create, name iaict-neon, direct Neon connection string) and shares the config id; then the binding is uncommented in wrangler.jsonc, the beta redeployed, and durable multi-request flows verified live. COMPLETED 2026-11-02: the Owner created the Hyperdrive config 'iaict-neon' (id 3cdbf0e61cfc4a078ea1f4790200a65f; direct connection string without channel_binding, caching disabled) in the dashboard; the binding is active in wrangler.jsonc and the beta now runs DURABLE: /health reports storage 'postgresql-hyperdrive'. Live verification with a temporary platform secret (deleted afterwards): tenant beta-pilot created in one request was fully usable in later requests - bootstrap admin, zone Z-01, mother plant MPL-001 referencing the zone, crop plan PLAN-2026 - with 5 audit entries readable through the API; records cross-checked present in Neon. One transient 500 on a list call was traced to the cached per-isolate connection pattern; WorkerPgStore now opens a fresh connection per operation (Cloudflare's prescribed Hyperdrive pattern) and repeated spaced calls all return 200. Seed records (beta-pilot tenant with its zone/plant/plan) intentionally remain in Neon as the beta's first real data. Platform administration stays disabled until the Owner sets their own PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY secret. URL CHANGE + ADMIN KEY (2026-11-02): the Owner renamed the account workers.dev subdomain from 'iaict-coreplatform-mhy' to 'mihy' - the canonical beta URL is now https://iaict-core-platform.mihy.workers.dev and the old URL no longer resolves; all data was unaffected (it lives in Neon, verified: beta-pilot records intact at the new address). The Owner also set their own PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY secret (verified active from outside: a wrong key now returns 401 PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID instead of 503).

Supabase trial executed at the Owner's direction (2026-11-02): the beta's Hyperdrive binding now points at a Supabase PostgreSQL project (Singapore, direct connection, config 'iaict-supabase' id 4ee90fdeba69436493d69e11fd7a870b); the schema was auto-created by the Worker on first request and the beta-pilot dataset was rebuilt from an API snapshot (tenant, Pilot Admin, zones Z-01 + Z-TMP, plant MPL-001, plan PLAN-2026). Neon (config 'iaict-neon') is untouched and remains the instant rollback. Measured result: latency improved (successful calls 5-6s vs 7-10s) but the failure rate did NOT improve (sequential 8/20, dashboard-parallel 19/48 - same class as Neon: 1101/1102/dropped connections). wrangler tail evidence (14 sampled requests: 9 ok, 4 canceled by the runtime's hang detector, 1 exceededCpu; successful requests burn ~1.2-1.9s CPU each) identifies the bottleneck as the Cloudflare Python Workers runtime itself (Pyodide + synchronous pg8000), not the database. DEC-006 is therefore amended in part: the database may be Neon or Supabase interchangeably, but the API runtime is expected to move to a plain always-on host (T-013) running the same ASGI app under uvicorn with the psycopg backend - the portability rules of DEC-006 are what make this a packaging change, not a rewrite. The Owner also forgot their PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY; a temporary secret was used to create the tenant on Supabase and deleted immediately after, so platform administration is disabled (503) until the Owner sets a fresh key of their own choosing.

Owner decision 2026-11-03: adopt Cloudflare D1 as the beta's store on Workers (T-014), superseding the T-013 plain-host relocation. This AMENDS DEC-006 in one respect: a Cloudflare-proprietary API (D1) now sits behind the store boundary. The rest of DEC-006's portability discipline is kept and is what bounds the lock-in: the store interface is storage-agnostic, the PostgreSQL backends (psycopg + pg8000/Hyperdrive) remain in the tree and green in tests, the datasets on Supabase and Neon are untouched, and wrangler.jsonc documents the rollback (restore the Hyperdrive binding + IAICT_BACKEND=hyperdrive + redeploy). Rationale is measured, not preferential: on the same free Python Workers runtime, D1 scored sequential 20/20 + parallel 48/48 with cpuTime median ~26-42ms per request, versus 8/20 + 19/48 at ~1,241ms CPU on PostgreSQL via Hyperdrive; the hang-cancellations and exceededCpu failures disappeared entirely. D1 was also verified to enforce the composite (tenant_id, ref_id) foreign keys the tenant isolation model relies on (cross-tenant INSERT rejected, SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY).
